COMPONENT KIT

  • Clay slab — the base card: 42 px radius, inner highlight + inner shade + warm drop shadow
  • Fingerprint grain — feTurbulence overlay in multiply so every surface looks hand-pressed
  • Clay numerals — Manrope 800 with stacked highlight / ledge shadows; the hero metric
  • Clay coil — a line chart drawn as a rolled worm of teal clay (thick round-cap stroke)
  • Sculpting stick — Pulse's pointer: a wooden tool that pokes the anomaly and leaves a dent
  • Press-in button — the human action; shadows flip inward and it sinks 6 px when chosen

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Squash & stretch landing — scaleY 0.82 → 1.06 → 1, elastic.out(1, .5), 0.5 s; contact frame sits on the downbeat (0.5 s = one beat at 120 BPM)
  • Stop-motion stutter — idle wobble of ±1 px / ±0.6° on steps(12) = animated on twos at 24 fps; keeps every slab alive between beats
  • Press-in — shadow inset flip + translateY 6 px, power2.out 0.12 s, landing on a snare so the human choice feels physical

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Clay makes a cold monitoring product feel warm and touchable, and one lumpy slab among smooth ones reads as “something's off” with zero copy. Risk: drifts childish if the palette goes pastel — keep the ink, teal and coral saturated and the numbers crisp.

Adapt to your product: Replace each slab with one of your product's cards (orders, builds, tickets); keep the numbers as real typeset text on the clay so they stay legible, and let only the problem card be lumpy and coral.
